pr_title: Fix Insteon config flow with add X10 and device override
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
The Insteon integration options flow allows for the addition of X10 devices and Insteon device overrides. The methods change `config_data` directly so HA does not recognize that a change has been made therefore the changes are not stored to `core.config_entries`. This change modifies a copy of `config_data` so that HA knows a change has been made when the comparison is performed in `config_entries.async_update_entry`.

issue_context.title: Insteon X10 additions only save a single element instead of adding to the JSON array
issue_context.body:

  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 

-->
  As reported in the forums,[https://community.home-assistant.io/t/x10-through-insteon-integration-no-longer-working/245818/5](url), since 2020.12.0 X10 devices added via the Insteon integration do not work.  As it was pointed out in the thread, an edit to the core.config_entries file resolves this by adding to the JSON array.

I haven't dug into the Insteon repository to pinpoint where this has happened, but since I just added my X10 devices in the past week it appears as though the command to add X10 devices just updates element 0 instead of appending to the JSON array.

In the core.config_entries, after adding a dozen X10 devices I see just one element:
```
                "options": {
                    "x10_devices": [
                        {
                            "housecode": "a",
                            "unitcode": 5,
                            "platform": "switch",
                            "dim_steps": 22
                        }                      
                    ]
                },    
```

But it should be (and I have manually edited to be this and it works):
```
                "options": {
                    "x10_devices": [
                        {
                            "housecode": "a",
                            "unitcode": 5,
                            "platform": "switch",
                            "dim_steps": 22
                        },
                        {
                            "housecode": "h",
                            "unitcode": 14,
                            "platform": "switch",
                            "dim_steps": 2
                        },
                        {
                            "housecode": "h",
                            "unitcode": 9,
                            "platform": "switch",
                            "dim_steps": 2
                        },
                        {
                            "housecode": "h",
                            "unitcode": 15,
                            "platform": "switch",
                            "dim_steps": 2
                        },
                        {
                            "housecode": "h",
                            "unitcode": 16,
                            "platform": "switch",
                            "dim_steps": 2
                        }                        
                    ]
                },
```

comments:
Hey there @teharris1, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`insteon`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L222) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>
OK, figured this one out. The same issue exists with device overrides by the way. A fix will be introduced in the next few days but I am not exactly sure when it will make it into a release.

review_comments:
Is there an opportunity to break `add_x10_device` and `add_device_override` into smaller units?

When I think about what they do, `add_x10_device` does a lot of things:

1. Iterates the current x10 config and finds only devices that are not the same house/unit code as the new one being added.
2. Creates the new device entry
3. Looks for `CONF_OVERRIDE` and copies it to the new config
4. Merges and returns the new config.

I realize that might not be possible with the current design, but I think its at least worth thinking about.

Yeah, you are right. The config entry should be a dict not a list, then I could use the key of the device address to change or add a config entry for that device without the logic of finding the same device in the list. Making this change would also require migrating the existing config to the new format as well, which would be removed at a later date.  But, this would have made a lot of things simpler (doh). 

That would require refactoring and make this PR much bigger. Since this fixes an existing bug I would like to move forward with the code as is and I will commit to putting that in my backlog and getting it done right away.
